outcome: No mathematical progress (proof, disproof, counterexample, or new verification bound) on the Kummer–Vandiver conjecture itself was found since 26 January 2024; the only related activity is a June–October 2025 addition of the open conjecture's formal statement (unproved, containing `sorry`) to DeepMind's formal-conjectures Lean repository.

ai.basis_quote: The theorem declaration includes `sorry`... the class number of the maximal real subfield of ℚ(ζₚ) is not divisible by p — the `sorry` at the end of the proof block confirms this is a research-level open problem being documented in the Formal Conjectures project, rather than an established result with a completed proof.

summary: The Kummer–Vandiver (Vandiver) conjecture states that no prime p divides the class number of the maximal real subfield of the p-th cyclotomic field. As of the frozen January 2024 Wikipedia revision, it was verified computationally for all primes below 2^31 (Hart, Harvey, Ong, 2017) and remained unproved, with Washington-style heuristics suggesting counterexamples (if any exist) are astronomically rare. Searches for a proof, disproof, counterexample, extended verification bound, or new theoretical advance directly settling any case of the conjecture since 26 January 2024 turned up nothing: general search engines return only pre-2024 material (the 2^31 verification, the 2020 'Vandiver's Conjecture via K-theory' preprint by Stolin/Ghate which itself remains an unpublished, non-digested attempt from 2020, Gras/Mihăilescu heuristic refinements, and the unrelated function-field analogue counterexamples, which are a genuinely different problem under §3.1's scope rule since they concern function fields rather than the classical cyclotomic-field statement). The only post-window item found anywhere near this problem is a June 2025 GitHub issue (#137) and an October 2025 merged pull request (#297) in DeepMind's 'formal-conjectures' repository, which added a Lean formal statement of the conjecture (file FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/KummerVandiver.lean) ending in `sorry` — i.e., a machine-checkable statement of the open conjecture with no proof attached. This is a formalisation of the problem statement, not a mathematical result, so per §6.2 it does not constitute AI involvement in a result (ai_role none, formalisation_only true) and does not move status off open. I also checked recent Iwasawa-theory literature (2024 Massey-product paper on Iwasawa λ-invariants, 2025 papers on λ/μ-invariants of real cyclotomic and quadratic fields) for any bearing on Vandiver's conjecture specifically; these are related-but-distinct results (bounds/criteria in adjacent settings) that do not settle any case of the stated conjecture, so they are excluded under the variant/related-problem rule in §3.1.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2020 Stolin/Ghate 'Vandiver's Conjecture via K-theory' preprint, if it were still under active revision or gained new commentary after January 2024, might count as `claimed` progress; however, no post-2024 update, endorsement, or digestion of that specific preprint was found, and it predates the window regardless, so it would be `open_stale` evidence at best, not a change in the measured window. The formal-conjectures repository entry could be read as 'AI lab engagement with the problem' worth noting even though it is formalisation-only; I have recorded it in `event`/`ai` fields for transparency while keeping ai_role as none per the explicit rule that formalisation-only work is not AI involvement in a result.
what_would_settle_it: A dated preprint or announcement (after 26 January 2024) claiming a proof, disproof, explicit counterexample, or an extended computational verification bound beyond 2^31 for the Kummer–Vandiver conjecture; or a completed (non-`sorry`) Lean proof of the KummerVandiver.lean statement in the formal-conjectures repository.
